text:
zoe.sales: LedgerOne just sent results from a 1h POC. They saw big throughput collapse during periodic bursts and p99s jumping to multiple seconds. They want a short explainer + config changes and impact on pricing/commit. Can we help?
hamid.sre: Paste their run details? qps curve, concurrency, model, seq lengths, batching mode, duration, warmup?
zoe.sales: Their test: 
  - model: open-redwood-7b-v1 (fp16)
  - pattern: steady 80 qps, every 10m a 2m burst up to 240 qps
  - clients: 40 parallel clients across two zones
  - input length: avg 90 tokens, 95th=400, some up to 1500 (long invoices)
  - batching: client-side only, no server batching configured
  - warmup: ~3m, total test 60m
hamid.sre: That profile is a classic tail scenario. Main drivers: very long outliers create batch skew; client-side batching prevents effective packing; KV cache churn for long sequences increases memory churn; also cross-zone client bursts can spike network egress and scheduling which shows up as high p99. Short warmup means GPUs may not reach steady clocks.
reed.ml: Model notes: open-redwood-7b-v1 int8 gives 2-3x throughput on standard infra but watch eval impact for invoice extraction tasks; sometimes numeric accuracy can be slightly affected. However batching + cache usually gives larger tail benefits than quant alone.
mira.se: Remediation plan to propose to LedgerOne: 
  1) enable server-side continuous batching (batch_timeout=8ms, max_batch=128)
  2) add session_id to requests so hot sessions get KV cache (can be disabled per-customer)
  3) enforce soft max_input=512 for latency-sensitive route, route >512 to async job
  4) extend warmup to 10m with same burst cadence before measurement window
  5) if p99/p999 targets strict, provision Dedicated pool (pinned GPUs) during POC
jules.sales-eng: Pricing/commit note: Hosted is lower upfront but variable; Dedicated with a 3-GPU pool for their expected load gives much more consistent p99 and predictable per-token compute after commit discounts. I can run a 90-day committed vs hosted TCO and post numbers.
sec-bot: Security checklist requested: where prompts and logs are stored, retention defaults, ability to opt out of server-side caching, support for SSO (SAML/SCIM), audit log exports, regional hosting options
mira.se: Security answers: KV cache entries are opaque binary model state; we can disable caching for PII-sensitive customers. Dedicated/Private mode keeps logs and traces in customer region and supports customer-managed KMS. We'll provide a one-page security summary for procurement.
hamid.sre: Test plan for the next measurement run (recommended): 
  - warmup: 0->80 qps over 6m, warmup hold 10m, then 3 burst cycles to 240 qps for 2m spaced every 10m
  - enable server batching (8ms), max_batch=128, enable KV caching for sessioned traffic
  - include 10-15% very long inputs but route them to a separate async tag for comparison
  - collect: p50/p90/p95/p99/p999, batch size histogram, gpu_util, mem_free, per-zone network latencies, per-request trace id
reed.ml: Quick curl example to flip batching/session id: 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"open-redwood-7b-v1-int8","prompt":"<invoice>","max_tokens":300,"session_id":"ledgerone-poc-03"}'
jules.sales-eng: I'll attach a short email-ready 3-bullet summary for their infra lead and run the commit pricing calc.
zoe.sales: loadtest summary from their runner: run_id=lg-20260320-07, failures=2 (timeouts), avg=160ms, p95=510ms, p99=1500ms, p999=3100ms
mira.se: Offer: we can run a managed POC where our SEs configure batching/cache and re-run within 24-72h and deliver Grafana snapshots + CSVs. That usually resolves tails for these patterns.
jules.sales-eng: I'll prepare a draft quote for a 3-month Dedicated pilot vs expected hosted spend and post by EOD tomorrow.
zoe.sales: Thanks everyone  I'll send LedgerOne the security one-pager, the three-bullet explainer, and propose the managed POC.
sec-bot: one-pager (security-summary.pdf) uploaded to shared drive (link)
zoe.sales: Closing loop with prospect now. Thanks all :rocket:
